root_cause.text: macvlan_get_size() in drivers/net/macvlan.c failed to reserve netlink attribute space for IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF, so macvlan_fill_info() could later overrun the estimated skb space when it conditionally emitted that attribute.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `+ nla_total_size(4) /* IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF */` to `macvlan_get_size()`, and the CVE description states that `macvlan_fill_info()` already does `nla_put_s32()` for `port->bc_cutoff != 1` but `macvlan_get_size()` “does not account for IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF,” causing `nla_put_s32()` to fail with `-EMSGSIZE` and prevent interface dumping.

commit 79cf79abce71eb7dbc40e2f3121048ca5405cb47
Author: Michael Braun <michael-dev@fami-braun.de>
Date:   Thu Sep 25 16:31:08 2014 +0200

    macvlan: add source mode
    
    This patch adds a new mode of operation to macvlan, called "source".
    It allows one to set a list of allowed mac address, which is used
    to match against source mac address from received frames on underlying
    interface.
    This enables creating mac based VLAN associations, instead of standard
    port or tag base
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is about failing to reserve netlink attribute space for IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF, but this commit’s code is adding unrelated source-mode attributes and does not contain any IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF logic. In the shown `macvlan_get_size()` the reserved space is for `IFLA_MACVLAN_MODE`, `IFLA_MACVLAN_FLAGS`, `IFLA_MACVLAN_MACADDR_COUNT`, and `macvlan_get_size_mac(vlan)` for `IFLA_MACVLAN_MACADDR` (`+ nla_total_size(4) /* IFLA_MACVLAN_MACADDR_COUNT */ + macvlan_get_size_mac(vlan) /* IFLA_MACVLAN_MACADDR */`), while `macvlan_fill_info()` emits those same fields (`nla_put_u32(...MACADDR_COUNT...)` and nested MACADDR data). Since the buggy attribute is absent here, the specific bug is not present in this function body, and the fix for that issue is also not shown.

Background:

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit d4bff72c8401e6f56194ecf455db70ebc22929e2
Author: Thomas Karlsson <thomas.karlsson@paneda.se>
Date:   Wed Dec 2 19:49:58 2020 +0100

    macvlan: Support for high multicast packet rate
    
    Background:
    Broadcast and multicast packages are enqueued for later processing.
    This queue was previously hardcoded to 1000.
    
    This proved insufficient for handling very high packet rates.
    This resulted in packet drops for multicast.
    While at the same time unicast worked fine.
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function bodies already reserve netlink space for both attributes that are relevant to the reported bug. In `macvlan_get_size()` the diff adds `+ nla_total_size(4) /* IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_QUEUE_LEN */` and `+ nla_total_size(4) /* IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_QUEUE_LEN_USED */`, and in `macvlan_fill_info()` it actually emits both with `nla_put_u32(skb, IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_QUEUE_LEN, vlan->bc_queue_len_req)` and `nla_put_u32(skb, IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_QUEUE_LEN_USED, port->bc_queue_len_used)`. The vulnerability root cause was a missing size reservation for `IFLA_MACVLAN_BC_CUTOFF`, but that attribute is not present in this commit's code at all. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent here, and the fix for that specific issue is also not the one shown in this snippet.
